packageRules.description: Renovate itself releases several times a day. It's baked into the ARC runner image (images/arc-runner/Dockerfile) just to validate renovate.json, and every bump rebuilds that image, so take it weekly.

instantlinux/nut-upsd tags are <nut version>-r<Alpine package revision> (e.g. 2.8.5-r1). Default docker versioning treats `-r1` as a fixed variant suffix and would never propose -r2 or 2.8.6-r0; regex versioning treats the revision as a build number instead.

docs.jakerobb.org builds with the mkdocs-material image in-cluster (manifests/docs/deployment.yaml) and with the PyPI package in CI (docs-site/requirements.txt). Bump both in one PR so CI checks the version the site will actually run.
nginx's even minor versions are the stable line and odd ones are mainline. The docs site's nginx tracks stable only.
InfluxDB stays on 2.x. NetworkOptimizer (manifests/network-optimizer/influxdb-deployment.yaml) queries only in Flux, which InfluxDB 3 dropped for SQL and InfluxQL.

customManagers.description: Tool versions pinned as env vars in GitHub Actions workflows (helm, kubeconform in lint.yml) via an explicit annotation comment on the line above.

Image tags pinned in an Application's valuesObject (Authelia; both democratic-csi releases' driver and CSI sidecar images), separately from the chart's targetRevision (which the argocd manager already tracks) — neither built-in manager sees a nested image.tag override, so this catches it via an explicit annotation comment.

Tool versions pinned as ARGs in the ARC runner image's Dockerfile (helm, kubectl, shellcheck, node, renovate, ...) via an explicit annotation comment on the line above, same pattern as the workflow env vars. The FROM line is handled by the built-in dockerfile manager.

ARC runner image (ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner) pinned in the arc-runners scale set's pod template, which neither built-in manager sees (it's nested under valuesObject). Annotation comment on the line above, same pattern as the others.

ArgoCD's own chart version is bumped by hand via the `helm install`/`helm upgrade` command documented in argocd/README.md (see 'Upgrading ArgoCD itself') — it isn't a Kubernetes/ArgoCD Application manifest the built-in managers scan, so this catches it via an explicit annotation comment, same pattern as the Authelia one above. A PR here only updates the doc; the actual `helm upgrade` against the cluster is still a manual step by design.
